# Terminal UNKNOWN-create cleanup receipt extension

This separate action runs only the fixed installed module
`python -I -m just_akash.scanner_v2_recovery_cleanup`. It preserves the published
known-identity cleanup action and delegates real deployment-ACK targets to the
original engine. The SDK cleanup workflow changes only its npm/action directory;
its caller inputs, native job/step identity, concurrency and secret scope remain.
A BB caller needs an explicit reviewed SDK pin update before using this version.

A terminal, latest-attempt producer with a complete immutable JIT ACK chain and
`lease_reconcile` NO_WIRE→UNKNOWN chain may produce READONLY_DERIVATION DATA.
The original UNKNOWN must already contain the official manifest version and
complete active/closed pre-create DSEQ baseline. The fixed Python resolver uses
the existing twice-complete Console snapshot, unique-new-candidate selector and
two-source signed creation/current-owner/group/version evidence. No caller DSEQ,
name or label selects a deployment. A derived target explicitly refers to UNKNOWN;
it has no manufactured deployment-ACK field.

The separate immutable derivation artifact is uploaded and exact-body read back
before either effect intent. Both NO_WIRE intents and the effect's acknowledged
UNKNOWN precede the actual inherited close/removal transport. Fresh native,
complete Console and signed creation proof are repeated at each final guard.
The original bound-owner wallet gate and height-pinned full deployment/lease/escrow
closure still apply. The one-use effect latch, no retry, exact RunnerID removal,
independent all-status registration absence checks and ACK-loss semantics are
inherited unchanged. Original producer UNKNOWN is never rewritten or upgraded.

Close/remove use the SAME `scanner-v2-RUN-aATTEMPT-rROUND-KIND` namespace as the
old schema. The complete native history reader accepts both effect schemas.
A later genuine deployment ACK may bridge a prior derived target only if its
parent is the exact original UNKNOWN and owner/DSEQ/JIT ID/group/version/baseline
match. Prior UNKNOWN/ACK still veto another wire of that kind. Missing executed
handler intents, incomplete inventories and untracked current process records HOLD.
Artifact names are not global CAS, and a deleted entire native run cannot be
reconstructed from the GitHub API. Whole-history visibility is a qualification
limit, not an exactly-once claim.

All artifact runtime credentials stay in the Node worker. Its Python child gets
only the existing hosted management credentials; none go into a tenant payload.
The official artifact client and lockfile are unchanged from the published action.
Its internal transport retries are bounded by the inherited 18-second worker and
20-second pipe deadlines. There is no caller-level artifact overwrite/retry or
effect replay. The native reader still caps each worker at 60 GETs; larger or
slower histories HOLD. The public synthetic full-phase counter is
19/47/45/47/47/47/47/47, not a measured GitHub latency result.

Unsupported: normal-mode UNKNOWN recovery, legacy UNKNOWN without recorded
baseline/version, deployment NO_WIRE-only, missing deployment record, JIT UNKNOWN
without returned ID, and unused pre-lease JIT registrations without a positive
terminal transport fence. Missing records/outputs never prove no deployment.
Real durability, signed endpoint compatibility, normal/terminal live effects,
end-to-end cleanup and rollout remain unqualified by source tests.

Offline checks use `npm test` with RUNNER_TEMP set. The separate actual FD/Node
supervisor control uses `PUBLIC_TEST_PYTHON` and
`node --test test_pipe.cjs`; its child startup is a disclosed test-only source
binding to the real new Pipe/Operation classes, and its only wire is a sentinel
file. Python source controls are `tests/test_scanner_v2_recovery_cleanup.py`.
No test contacts GitHub, Console, chain, registry or a provider.
